intent: A counting quiz that turns into a border story: bars put the three giant-peak nations to scale, a BORDER / INSIDE split shows that most of Nepal's giants stand on a frontier line, and a pin lands on the tallest of all with the metre-exact height both countries agreed.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: How many 8,000-metre peaks stand in NEPAL?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: How many 8,000-metre peaks stand in nepal?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: 8. More giant peaks than any other country, packed into a thin strip of Himalaya.

lines.direction: ease back along the range; three bars rise on 'Pakistan' with Nepal on top; the Pakistani flag-ball thinks on 'Pakistan'; a mountain sticker on 'line' as Nepal pulses
lines.text: Pakistan comes next, home of K2. China shares most of its giants across a border line.

lines.direction: tighten on the central Himalaya; the SHARED / ALL NEPAL split lands on 'straddle' with the frontier tag; a flag sticker on 'India'; a boot sticker on 'inside' as Nepal pulses
lines.text: Most of Nepal's giants straddle the frontier with China or India. A few rise entirely inside the country.

lines.direction: drift east to the Khumbu; the Everest pin and the 8,849 m card on 'Everest' with a snow sticker; a plane sticker on 'airstrip' as the Nepali flag-ball grins and Nepal pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: The tallest of all, Everest, sits right on the China line. Climbers from the south begin at a mountain airstrip.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: A country of giants. Follow us.
